chunk_findings.detail: The new `sweep_interval_s` knob defaults to 900 seconds, but the old behavior—stated in the knob’s own doc as “0 sweeps on every brief, as before”—was to run `dispose_finished` on every `brief`. On an upgraded repo with finished leftover worktrees and no `.ddflow/local/sweep-finished.last`, `ddflow brief` will now skip the sweep for up to 15 minutes instead of sweeping immediately. This violates [r-everything-configurable], which requires a new knob to default to the old behavior; the default should be 0 (with cadence opt-in).

chunk_findings.detail: `prefetch_on_base` runs `git rev-list --no-walk <chunk> ^<base> --` and treats every printed object id as “base lacks this commit.” But `--no-walk` deliberately does not traverse ancestors of a negative revision: if `<A>` is an ancestor of `<base>`, `git rev-list --no-walk <A> ^<base>` still prints `<A>`. So a worktree whose HEAD is `<A>`, already reachable from the base, leads `prefetch_on_base(["<A>"], "<base>")` to cache `_on_base[(<A>, <base>)]` as `False`, and a later `on_base("<A>", "<base>")` returns `False` when the true answer is `True` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <A> <base>` exits 0). The code comment’s claim that this prints “exactly the listed commits the base lacks” is false, and the wrong reachability answer can drive an incorrect finished/sweep classification.

chunk_findings.detail: With the new default `lease.scan_view_trees_max = 16` and the stated 126 stale leases in the falsifier, `_measure` will measure 16 worktrees. For each measured tree it calls `W.tree_work(wt, base, ahead=False)` for dirty files and then `facts.ahead(wt, base)` for the ahead count. Those are two git subprocesses per measured tree, so just these calls produce 32 subprocesses before the initial `RepoFacts` queries. That makes the change's own falsifier "more than 30 git subprocesses for status with 126 stale leases" true, not false.

A repository with 17 stale worktrees therefore changes from measuring all 17 to measuring 16 and marking the 17th as NOT MEASURED. That is not the old behaviour, contradicting the change's CONFORMANCE claim that "a new knob defaults to the old behaviour"; it is a semantic behaviour change for existing users, not merely additive.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `sweep_interval_s` knob defaults to `900`, but its own doc says `0` is the old behaviour (“0 sweeps on every brief, as before”), and the change’s CONFORMANCE clause claims “a new knob defaults to the old behaviour.” Concrete failure: on an existing project after upgrading with no config change, `ddflow brief` no longer sweeps finished worktrees on every call. chunk_findings.detail: `on_base` collapses an unknown result into `False`. When `git merge-base --is-ancestor sha base` exits 128 (for example `sha` is an unknown object or not a commit), `on_base` returns `False`, which means "sha is not on base". That contradicts the module docstring's stated contract "An answer git could not give is ``None`` / -1, never a guess: unknown is not zero." A caller that uses `False` to decide whether scanning is unnecessary will act as though the commit is absent rather than unavailable, and the unknown key is not cached, so repeated unknown queries respawn subprocesses too.

chunk_findings.detail: `gather` and `inspect` declare `view: bool = False` and `_expired` forwards that value to `L.scan(..., view=view)`. Any call that uses the fallback path (`recoveries=None`)—for example an existing call `healthwatch.gather(log, st, cfg, repo, now)`—passes `False` as `L.scan`'s `view`. This breaks every legacy call site that has not yet been changed to pass `recoveries`.

chunk_findings.detail: The diff changes both `_measure` and `_note_landed` calls to pass extra positional arguments (`facts` and `budget`) — e.g. `_measure(rec, repo, cfg, facts, budget)` — but this part contains no corresponding update to the definitions of `_measure`/`_note_landed`; they retain their previous signatures (`_measure(rec, repo, cfg)` and `_note_landed(rec, it, state, cfg, repo)`). chunk_findings.detail: The new guard `return now - float(_sweep_stamp_path(repo).read_text().strip()) >= every` only catches `OSError`/`ValueError`, but a corrupt stamp containing `"nan"` parses successfully without raising. `float("nan")` produces NaN, so `now - NaN >= every` is always `False`, making `_sweep_due` return `False` on every call and permanently preventing `CL.sweep_finished` from running for that repo. chunk_findings.detail: `RepoFacts.on_base` checks `r.code not in (0, 1)` and then returns `False` on line 128 when the code is outside `(0, 1)`. But line 130 returns `r.ok` (which means `r.code == 0`), meaning that any non-zero exit code except those not in `(0, 1)` falls through to line 130 where `r.ok` is `False`, which correctly returns `False`. However, when `r.code` is something like 128 (unknown commit), line 128 returns `False` and caches `self._on_base[key] = False`, treating an unknown commit as "not an ancestor" rather than an error or unknown state, contradicting the docstring comment which says "unknown: not remembered".

chunk_findings.detail: `gather` and `inspect` declare `view: bool = False` and `_expired` forwards that value to `L.scan(..., view=view)`. In this same change `L.scan`'s `view` is not a boolean switch: it is the precomputed `gitbatch.RepoFacts` batching object added in `ddflow/infra/gitbatch.py` (the object governed by the new `lease.scan_view_trees_max`/`lease.scan_view_verdicts_max` limits). Any call that uses the fallback path (`recoveries=None`)—for example an existing call `healthwatch.gather(log, st, cfg, repo, now)`—passes `False` as `L.scan`'s `view`. Because `False` is not `None`, `L.scan` will treat `False` as an already-built `RepoFacts` object and then access its tree/verdict fields on a bool, raising `AttributeError`/`TypeError`. This breaks every legacy call site that has not yet been changed to pass `recoveries`.

chunk_findings.detail: The diff changes both `_measure` and `_note_landed` calls to pass extra positional arguments (`facts` and `budget`) — e.g. `_measure(rec, repo, cfg, facts, budget)` — but this part contains no corresponding update to the definitions of `_measure`/`_note_landed`; they retain their previous signatures (`_measure(rec, repo, cfg)` and `_note_landed(rec, it, state, cfg, repo)`). chunk_findings.detail: The new guard `return now - float(_sweep_stamp_path(repo).read_text().strip()) >= every` only catches `OSError`/`ValueError`, but a corrupt stamp containing `"nan"` parses successfully without raising. `float("nan")` produces NaN, so `now - NaN >= every` is always `False`, making `_sweep_due` return `False` on every call and permanently preventing `CL.sweep_finished` from running for that repo. The previous code did not return `False` in that case; it would overwrite the corrupt stamp and perform the sweep. Concrete input: `.ddflow/local/sweep-finished.last` contains `nan\n`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py:_sweep_due

chunk_findings.detail: `RepoFacts.on_base` checks `r.code not in (0, 1)` and then returns `False` on line 128 when the code is outside `(0, 1)`. But line 130 returns `r.ok` (which means `r.code == 0`), meaning that any non-zero exit code except those not in `(0, 1)` falls through to line 130 where `r.ok` is `False`, which correctly returns `False`. However, when `r.code` is something like 128 (unknown commit), line 128 returns `False` and caches `self._on_base[key] = False`, treating an unknown commit as "not an ancestor" rather than an error or unknown state, contradicting the docstring comment which says "unknown: not remembered".
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/gitbatch.py:127

chunk_findings.detail: The stamp is written only after `CL.sweep_finished` returns, so a sweep that raises leaves no fresh stamp. With `worktree.sweep_interval_s=900` and no previous stamp, a first `brief` attempts the full sweep; if `CL.sweep_finished` consistently raises—for example a finished worktree whose branch cannot be deleted causes it to throw after issuing its git calls—then every later `brief` sees `_sweep_due` return `True` and runs the same failing, expensive sweep. The previous code wrote the stamp *before* the sweep precisely so a sweep that died was not retried on every call. This makes the interval ineffective exactly when the sweep is most costly, defeating the change’s stated [R-scalability] goal that `sweep_finished` runs on cadence, not in every brief.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `sweep_interval_s` knob defaults to `900`, but its own doc says `0` is the old behaviour (“0 sweeps on every brief, as before”), and the change’s CONFORMANCE clause claims “a new knob defaults to the old behaviour.” Concrete failure: on an existing project after upgrading with no config change, `ddflow brief` no longer sweeps finished worktrees on every call. Run `brief`, finish a worktree, run `brief` again within 900 seconds; the second run skips the sweep it would have performed before this change, leaving the leftover worktree until the interval elapses. The default should be `0` to preserve old behaviour, or the conformance claim is false.

chunk_findings.detail: `on_base` collapses an unknown result into `False`. When `git merge-base --is-ancestor sha base` exits 128 (for example `sha` is an unknown object or not a commit), `on_base` returns `False`, which means "sha is not on base". That contradicts the module docstring's stated contract "An answer git could not give is ``None`` / -1, never a guess: unknown is not zero." A caller that uses `False` to decide whether scanning is unnecessary will act as though the commit is absent rather than unavailable, and the unknown key is not cached, so repeated unknown queries respawn subprocesses too.

chunk_findings.detail: The cited probe only demonstrates that the new caps reduce git subprocess count; it does not show old behavior is preserved. The new defaults (`16`, `0`) are not the old behavior: before, `status`/`brief` measured every stale worktree and weighed every merged-but-unfinished item, and this knob’s upgrade-safety claim requires the default to retain that. Concrete failure: a repo with 17 stale clean worktrees under an unconfigured upgrade now reports the 17th as NOT MEASURED rather than measuring it, and `scan_view_verdicts_max=0` disables the prior full verdict scan.

chunk_findings.detail: `RepoFacts._tip_aheads` passes `base` straight into git’s `%(ahead-behind:{base})` atom, but that atom requires a full ref name (`refs/heads/main`). `RepoFacts.base` returns `configured` unchanged and, for the default path, `W.default_branch` returns the short branch name (`main`), not `refs/heads/main`. For the common case `facts.ahead(path, "main")`, `git for-each-ref --format=%(objectname) %(ahead-behind:main) refs/heads` exits nonzero, so `_tips["main"]` stays empty and `ahead` falls back to one `git rev-list --count main..<head>` per distinct worktree HEAD. A status scan over 126 stale leases whose worktrees point at 31 or more distinct branch tips then spawns more than 30 git subprocesses, contradicting this change’s FALSIFIER and the module docstring’s “one for-each-ref per command”.

A repo with 17 stale clean worktrees and no config change will no longer have the 17th tree measured on upgrade, so the upgrade note misclassifies this as additive. The triage probe (`test_status_with_126_stale_leases_spawns_few_processes`) does not answer this: it passes by exercising the 16-tree cap and counting subprocesses, not by verifying that a 17th stale clean worktree is still measured.

chunk_findings.detail: The test’s own docstring says an unknown commit is “could not tell”, not “not an ancestor”, yet it asserts `f.on_base("0" * 40, "main") is False`. In this tri-state API `False` is the off-base value; the correct unknown result must be `None` (the module docstring says unknown is never a guess). This test therefore codifies the bug from previous finding 2 and would fail once `on_base` returns `None` for exit 128. The author’s probe passes only because the production code returns the `False` this test demands, not because the contract is met.

chunk_findings.detail: `RepoFacts.on_base` checks `r.code not in (0, 1)` on line 127 and returns `False` on line 128 when true. However, line 128 returns `False` which exits the function immediately, so the subsequent cache assignment `self._on_base[key] = r.ok` on line 131 is correctly skipped for non-zero/non-one codes, but the return statement on line 128 returns `False`, which means "is an ancestor" returns `False` (meaning "not on base") when `git merge-base --is-ancestor` fails with 128 (unknown commit). A caller querying `on_base` for a non-existent or unknown commit receives `False` instead of an indication of failure or unavailability, causing the system to treat an unknown commit as definitively not an ancestor.

chunk_findings.detail: The triage probe only runs the status/subprocess-count test and does not call `brief` twice within the interval, so it does not answer the original defect. The default is still `900`, while the old behavior—and this knob’s own docs for `0`—was to sweep finished worktrees on every `brief`. Concrete failure: on an existing project with no config change, run `brief`, finish a worktree, run `brief` again within 900 seconds; the second run skips the sweep it would have performed before the upgrade, contradicting the change’s stated CONFORMANCE “a new knob defaults to the old behaviour” [r-upgrade-safe].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/worktree.py:sweep_interval_s

chunk_findings.detail: The cited probe only demonstrates that the new caps reduce git subprocess count; it does not show old behavior is preserved. The new defaults (`16`, `0`) are not the old behavior: before, `status`/`brief` measured every stale worktree and weighed every merged-but-unfinished item, and this knob’s upgrade-safety claim requires the default to retain that. Concrete failure: a repo with 17 stale clean worktrees under an unconfigured upgrade now reports the 17th as NOT MEASURED rather than measuring it, and `scan_view_verdicts_max=0` disables the prior full verdict scan.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/lease.py:scan_view_trees_max / scan_view_verdicts_max

chunk_findings.detail: `RepoFacts._tip_aheads` passes `base` straight into git’s `%(ahead-behind:{base})` atom, but that atom requires a full ref name (`refs/heads/main`). `RepoFacts.base` returns `configured` unchanged and, for the default path, `W.default_branch` returns the short branch name (`main`), not `refs/heads/main`. For the common case `facts.ahead(path, "main")`, `git for-each-ref --format=%(objectname) %(ahead-behind:main) refs/heads` exits nonzero, so `_tips["main"]` stays empty and `ahead` falls back to one `git rev-list --count main..<head>` per distinct worktree HEAD. A status scan over 126 stale leases whose worktrees point at 31 or more distinct branch tips then spawns more than 30 git subprocesses, contradicting this change’s FALSIFIER and the module docstring’s “one for-each-ref per command”.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/gitbatch.py:_tip_aheads

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding #6 still holds. `new = "16"` plus `impact = "additive"` does not preserve the old behaviour [r-upgrade-safe]: before this change `status`/`brief` measured every stale worktree, while `_measure` now stops after the budget (`lease.scan_view_trees_max`) is exhausted and marks the rest `salvageable = None` / NOT MEASURED. A repo with 17 stale clean worktrees and no config change will no longer have the 17th tree measured on upgrade, so the upgrade note misclassifies this as additive. The triage probe (`test_status_with_126_stale_leases_spawns_few_processes`) does not answer this: it passes by exercising the 16-tree cap and counting subprocesses, not by verifying that a 17th stale clean worktree is still measured.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.lease.scan_view_trees_max.toml:6 and :8

chunk_findings.detail: The new `worktree.sweep_interval_s` knob defaults to `900`, but the old `brief` swept finished worktrees on every invocation. The change’s own CONFORMANCE text requires “a new knob defaults to the old behaviour” [r-upgrade-safe], and this note says the old per-call sweep is restored only by setting `0`; `impact = "additive"` therefore misclassifies a user-visible behavior change. Concrete failure: on an existing project upgraded with no config change, run `brief`, finish a worktree, then run `brief` again within 900 seconds; the second run skips the sweep the prior code would have performed. The triage probe `test_status_with_126_stale_leases_spawns_few_processes` counts subprocess spawns and does not exercise the sweep cadence, so it does not answer this.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.worktree.sweep_interval_s.toml:6,8

chunk_findings.detail: The new `lease.scan_view_verdicts_max` knob defaults to `0`, which disables the previous status/brief full verdict scan. This violates the CONFORMANCE requirement that a new knob default to the old behaviour [r-upgrade-safe]; the note’s own `why` says status and brief “no longer weigh the full completion” and “set above 0 to restore it”, so it is a behavior change, not `impact = "additive"`. Concrete failure: on an existing project with a merged-but-unfinished lease, run `status` after upgrading with no config change; it no longer weighs completion for any item, whereas the pre-change `status` did. The triage probe `test_status_with_126_stale_leases_spawns_few_processes` only checks process counts and does not answer this.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.lease.scan_view_verdicts_max.toml:6,8

chunk_findings.detail: The test’s own docstring says an unknown commit is “could not tell”, not “not an ancestor”, yet it asserts `f.on_base("0" * 40, "main") is False`. In this tri-state API `False` is the off-base value; the correct unknown result must be `None` (the module docstring says unknown is never a guess). This test therefore codifies the bug from previous finding 2 and would fail once `on_base` returns `None` for exit 128. The author’s probe passes only because the production code returns the `False` this test demands, not because the contract is met.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_git_batch.py:test_an_unknown_commit_is_not_reported_as_off_the_base

chunk_findings.detail: These tests assert that two immediate `LC.brief` runs on an unconfigured repo invoke `sweep_finished` only once (`len(calls) == 1`). That can only be true if the new `worktree.sweep_interval_s` default is positive. The change’s CONFORMANCE clause requires “a new knob defaults to the old behaviour”, and the previous `brief` swept finished worktrees on every call, so the default must be `0`. The author’s triage for previous finding 9 only runs the status subprocess-count probe, which does not exercise this default; the upgrade-safety violation remains and these tests lock it in.

chunk_findings.detail: `RepoFacts.on_base` checks `r.code not in (0, 1)` on line 127 and returns `False` on line 128 when true. However, line 128 returns `False` which exits the function immediately, so the subsequent cache assignment `self._on_base[key] = r.ok` on line 131 is correctly skipped for non-zero/non-one codes, but the return statement on line 128 returns `False`, which means "is an ancestor" returns `False` (meaning "not on base") when `git merge-base --is-ancestor` fails with 128 (unknown commit). A caller querying `on_base` for a non-existent or unknown commit receives `False` instead of an indication of failure or unavailability, causing the system to treat an unknown commit as definitively not an ancestor.

chunk_findings.detail: The call to `W.tree_work(wt, base, ahead=False)` on line 279 passes a keyword argument `ahead=False` that is unsupported by `W.tree_work`. `W.tree_work` is defined elsewhere as taking `(wt, base)` (without an `ahead` parameter), so calling it with `ahead=False` raises an immediate `TypeError` whenever `_measure` evaluates an unmeasured tree.
